items.title: No local measure of completion or alert response
items.whyItMatters: The centre cannot say who is dropping out or how long alerts wait, although both are the likely failure points (claims c2 and c4).
items.opportunity: Define completion per patient and time to nurse contact from the platform export and report them monthly.

items.title: Why patients stop is known only from other centres
items.whyItMatters: Reasons for stopping (claim c3) may differ here, where older and rural patients are common.
items.opportunity: Interview patients who stopped, sampled by age, deprivation and clinic.

items.title: Patients needing an interpreter are missing from the evidence
items.whyItMatters: The interview study had almost no participants needing an interpreter.
items.opportunity: Offer interviews with professional interpreters and report completion by preferred language.

items.title: Weekend alert handling
items.whyItMatters: Slow weekend response may drive dropout (claims c4 and c6).
items.opportunity: Analyse completion after weekday and weekend alerts separately.

items.title: Falling completion may partly mean improving symptoms
items.whyItMatters: Not every missed report is disengagement.
items.opportunity: Ask patients who stopped whether symptoms had settled, and compare with their last reported scores.

errorsFound: The need asks whether the programme is working; the retrieved trials already answer whether it can work, so a new local trial would repeat that question rather than answer the delivery question.
reevaluation: The gaps point to measuring and explaining delivery (completion, alert response, reasons for stopping) rather than re-estimating effectiveness.
summary: Five gaps; the missing local measures and the unexplained dropout are high severity.
